baseline_models.focus_anchor: The refusal to enter, its unlimited time phrase, the occupants' continued presence, and the speakers' sitting here form one construction.
baseline_models.mechanism: The absolute future refusal is reinforced by two duration roots and closed by a deictic sitting-position. The occupants' continued presence becomes the clock that keeps the speakers fixed outside.

activation_trace.role: Crossing into an interior supplies the threshold that the speakers categorically block.
Unbounded duration hardens a present objection into an unlimited refusal.
Continuity and stability make the occupants' presence the sustaining condition of non-entry.
Fixed sitting gives the temporal refusal a declared spatial endpoint here.

changed_reading.before: The group says it will not enter while the occupants remain.
changed_reading.after: The group constructs a self-renewing spatial-temporal lock: their staying there licenses our staying here without end.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: Go, you and your Lord, then fight, is set against the collective declaration that we are sitting here.
baseline_models.mechanism: A singular command of motion expands to a dual command of combat, while the first-person plural reserves only immobility. The utterance partitions motion, sovereignty, and conflict onto an addressed pair and nonparticipation onto the speakers.

activation_trace.role: Directed departure supplies the motion assigned away from the speaking group.
Lordship and sovereignty identify the second member of the externally assigned agent pair.
Reciprocal combat is the difficult action transferred to the dual subject.
Abstention from action defines the only role the plural speakers retain.

changed_reading.before: The speakers taunt Moses and decline to fight.
changed_reading.after: The speakers redraw the agency map: Moses and his Lord own movement and conflict, while the collective claims nonparticipation as its chosen function.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: They said, we will never enter, and we are sitting repeats emphatic first-person collective assertion.
baseline_models.mechanism: The speech root can carry an adopted position, while repeated first-person emphasis, absolute negation, imperative redirection, and final sitting make the utterance constitutive rather than merely descriptive. The group speaks itself into a stable policy.

activation_trace.role: Speech as an adopted belief or position lets the utterance establish collective policy.
Remaining without departure gives the spoken policy the shape of permanent residence outside.
Withdrawal from action is the concrete practice created by the declaration.

changed_reading.before: The verse reports a frightened reaction.
changed_reading.after: The verse records a performative counter-position by which the collective institutes refusal and inactivity as its policy.

context_deltas.mechanism: Earlier collective speech binds hearing to obedience inside a remembered covenant, and covenant-breaking is later imaged as undoing what was fastened. The focus repeats collective speech but replaces receptive action with emphatic non-entry and sitting, so its declaration reads as a counter-pledge.

activation_trace.role: The focus utterance establishes the group's adopted position.
The confirmed bond frames the earlier first-person response as covenant performance.
Hearing as understanding and compliance supplies the receptive half of the prior response.
Willing obedience supplies the action commitment that the focus speech reverses.
Undoing a bound structure provides the packet's explicit mechanism for covenant breach.

structural_cues: 5:7 embeds a first-person hearing-and-obedience response in remembered covenant language; 5:24 repeats first-person collective speech with non-entry and sitting.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies covenant, compliance, and unbinding images; I infer that the focus declaration functions as a counter-pledge. A live alternative is that it remains a situational refusal rather than a formally intended covenant act.

changed_reading.before: Their words are an immediate refusal under pressure.
changed_reading.after: Their words invert the remembered covenant response: instead of hearing that becomes action, speech now binds the group to non-action.

context_deltas.mechanism: The land is assigned and entry is commanded; the objectors make enemy exit the prerequisite of their entry; the two advisers instead make gate-entry the antecedent of victory. The focus escalates the objectors' sequence into an unlimited refusal, reversing the packet's threshold causality.

activation_trace.role: The focus blocks passage into the assigned interior.
The same threshold action appears as the initiating command.
An inscribed determination gives the destination prior authorization and obligation.
Passage outward is made by the objectors into the condition that must precede their own crossing inward.
The gate reduces an indefinite territorial problem to a concrete point of entry.
Prevailing force is presented as the result after crossing, not the prerequisite before it.

structural_cues: The sequence runs from the entry command in 5:21, through exit-before-entry in 5:22, to entry-before-victory in 5:23, and finally to unlimited non-entry in 5:24.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies the ordered threshold, exit, and victory clauses; I supply the causal comparison that the advisers treat crossing as enabling victory while the speakers reverse that arrow. The live alternative is ordinary tactical disagreement without a broader threshold mechanism.

changed_reading.before: The group refuses entry because the enemy still occupies the land.
changed_reading.after: The group reverses the offered strategy: it demands victory's result before crossing the threshold that the packet presents as victory's enabling act.

context_deltas.mechanism: The packet acknowledges coercive opponents and expected harm, yet the two men associated with fear advocate entry and attach action to reliance and secure trust. Fear is therefore not mechanically equivalent to sitting; the focus converts a real threat into a collective policy of abdication.

activation_trace.role: Withdrawal from action is the focus response whose relation to fear is being tested.
Coercive domination preserves the reality of the threat rather than dismissing it.
Anticipation of harm remains present in the very agents who recommend movement.
Reliance supplies a way to act under danger without claiming that danger is absent.
Settled trust is made the condition for acting through the threatened threshold.

structural_cues: The two men described with the fear construction in 5:23 issue an entry imperative, whereas the plural speakers in 5:24 announce sitting.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies threat, fear, reliance, and trust; I infer that it separates fear from paralysis and makes sitting a chosen response. The phrase about those who fear can alternatively refer to fear of God rather than fear of the opponents, which limits confidence but preserves the contrast.

changed_reading.before: The people sit because they are afraid of overpowering opponents.
changed_reading.after: The context allows fear and forward action to coexist, so the focus sitting is not fear's automatic consequence but the group's selected handling of fear.

context_deltas.mechanism: The group is reminded of favor and royal agency, but in the focus it transfers combat to a dual pair and sits collectively. Immediately afterward Moses can claim control only over his own self and brother and asks for separation. Endowed collective capacity contracts to an isolated dyad.

activation_trace.role: The dual combat command concentrates collective action in an assigned pair.
The plural group simultaneously withdraws itself from action.
A remembered good condition supplies the background of bestowed capacity.
Royal authority marks the group as recipients of public agency rather than passive dependents.
Possessive control narrows after the refusal to the minimal sphere Moses can still govern.
The self as one's own identity defines the first surviving unit of agency.
Brotherhood supplies the second and only other retained human bond.
Separation makes the contraction of the agentive collective explicit.

structural_cues: 5:20 addresses a favored people made kings; 5:24 opposes a dual combat verb to plural sitting; 5:25 leaves Moses naming only self and brother.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies bestowed kingship, dual grammar, narrowed possession, and separation; I infer a contraction of political and moral agency across the sequence. A live alternative is that kingship names status or freedom without implying practical military capacity.

changed_reading.before: The group merely outsources one dangerous task to Moses.
changed_reading.after: The refusal performs collective self-divestiture: a people named as kings abandons its agency until only a separated pair remains governable.

context_deltas.mechanism: The packet opens by carefully regulating release from prohibition, then describes the land as assigned to the people. The focus nonetheless treats enemy presence as an unofficial bar to entry; the next ayah turns that self-authored bar into an actual imposed prohibition.

activation_trace.role: Refused crossing is the action that the speakers treat as practically unavailable.
Unlimited duration gives their practical bar the force of a self-declared prohibition.
Release from a restriction establishes the packet's controlled legal boundary vocabulary.
Binding determination marks the land as assigned before the group bars itself from it.
Explicit prevention converts the group's chosen non-entry into an externally imposed exclusion.

structural_cues: The speakers' unlimited conditional refusal in 5:24 stands between the land written for them in 5:21 and its explicit prohibition to them in 5:26.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies legal boundary roots before and after the focus; I infer that the emphatic conditional functions like an unauthorized self-ban that returns as a real ban. The live alternative is that the focus language is only strategic refusal, with no legal coloring.

changed_reading.before: They decline access to a place currently controlled by others.
changed_reading.after: They convert assigned access into a self-authored exclusion, which the following ayah reverses back upon them as actual prohibition.

context_deltas.mechanism: The focus seeks stable non-movement here for as long as the others remain there, while assigning directed movement away. The sequel fixes a forty-year term and supplies wandering without destination: refusal of purposeful motion produces compulsory motion without arrival.

activation_trace.role: Unlimited duration supplies the speakers' chosen time horizon.
Continuance fixes their refusal to the other group's continued occupancy.
Purposeful departure is assigned to Moses rather than undertaken by the speakers.
Fixed sitting names the spatial condition the speakers choose for themselves.
Prevention removes the intended destination and turns movement into exclusion.
The number four supplies the counted frame of the forty-year consequence.
Years replace the speakers' unlimited horizon with a measured but extended term.

structural_cues: The branchless wandering root at 5:26 word 7 supplies motion without arrival and is retained here only as a structural cue.
The deictic opposition between there and here in 5:24 is followed by wandering in the land in 5:26.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies chosen sitting, delegated going, a fixed term, prohibition, and branchless wandering; I infer a spatial-temporal reversal in which rejected directed motion becomes imposed undirected motion. A live alternative is to read the sequel only as penalty, without treating its form as an inversion of the focus.

changed_reading.before: They choose to remain still and are later sentenced to wander.
changed_reading.after: Their attempted permanence reverses into motion without progress: by refusing the directed crossing, they lose both stable residence and reachable destination.

surprising_valid_outliers.containment: This is surprising because a second-person possessive can be ordinary direct address and does not itself deny shared lordship. It remains anchored in the focus's possessive Lord construction, favors addressed to the group, Moses's first-person Lord construction, and the ensuing separation. Downstream prose should render it only as rhetorical distancing or relational secession, never as a doctrinal denial.
surprising_valid_outliers.focus_anchor: The speakers say your Lord when assigning combat to Moses, whereas Moses says my Lord immediately after their refusal.

activation_trace.role: Sovereign lordship is grammatically placed on the addressed side of the agency partition.
Favor addressed to the whole group keeps them inside the prior relation that their wording appears to distance.
Bestowed good upon the two active men sharpens the contrast between received relation and chosen response.
Moses reclaims the nurturing relation in first-person address after the group has pushed it toward him.
Explicit separation gives the possible rhetorical distancing a visible relational outcome.

changed_reading.before: Your Lord is simply the normal possessive used while addressing Moses.
changed_reading.after: Exploratorily, the possessive helps push Lordship onto Moses's side, verbally seceding from a relation whose gifts had included the whole group.

surprising_valid_outliers.containment: This is branch-distant because the ordinary focus form denotes sitting, not a well. It remains worth carrying because the supplied sitting-root inventory includes a well abandoned before reaching water, while the context presents a gate and victory just beyond attempted entry. Render it only as a material analogy for stopping before the enabling threshold, not as lexical substitution or translation.
surprising_valid_outliers.focus_anchor: The final sitting term carries a rare branch image of excavation stopped before its goal.

activation_trace.role: An unfinished well abandoned before water models cessation immediately short of a sought resource.
The gate supplies the concrete threshold at which the collective stops.
Promised prevailing force supplies the result represented as lying beyond that threshold.

changed_reading.before: Their sitting is simple inactivity before a dangerous entry.
changed_reading.after: As a contained material analogy, their sitting resembles abandoning a well just before water: they stop at the gate before testing the action linked to victory.

strongest_changes: The focus speech becomes a counter-pledge that reverses the packet's remembered hearing-and-obedience formula.
The speakers reverse threshold causality by requiring enemy exit before entry, while the advisers place entry before victory.
A favored people named as kings contracts its agency until Moses can name only himself and his brother.
Chosen sitting and unlimited refusal reverse into measured years of wandering without arrival.
summary.what_was_special: The focus tightly couples speech, duration, deictic space, and number: emphatic plural refusal immobilizes here, assigns a moving and fighting dual elsewhere, and is then answered by separation, prohibition, and wandering.
remaining_uncertainties: The referent and force of the fear construction in 5:23 leave more than one route to the fear-versus-paralysis contrast.
The possessive your Lord can support rhetorical distancing but cannot by itself establish theological disavowal.
The abandoned-well image is a packet-licensed material analogy whose distance from the ordinary sitting sense requires explicit containment.
